db_evidence.notes: The memory DB (episodes/semantic_triples/event_steps/topic_facts) records the BOSS's own transformations (mahu boss: humanoid -> golden thorned chariot -> darker serpentine form, 72090-72240) and the post-fight loot drop ('阳炎珠' at 72240-72270, whose Chinese name 阳炎 ~ 'sun-flame/heat-haze' is the plausible etymological source of the English label 'Golden Haze'), but never states the PLAYER's transformation name anywhere in any table. A full-text search across episodes and visual_clips for all six literal option words returned zero rows (verified via rollout-01's own run_sql, and independently plausible given the caption text only describes 'fire-based attacks' generically). So the correct answer is not retrievable from text/SQL at all; it is only inferable either (a) by reading an on-screen skill/name label the frame extraction never captured, or (b) by outside knowledge of the game's spirit-form naming, or (c) by chance.

root_causes: The DB never records the player transformation's name in any structured or caption text, forcing every rollout onto clip_qa as the sole evidence source for this specific fact.

3 of 5 rollouts (00, 03, 04) correctly located the true transformation moment (within or adjacent to clue_interval 72210-72223) and accurately described a red/orange fire aura, but the visual sub-agent then chose the multiple-choice option by naive color-word matching ('red/orange' -> 'crimson tide') rather than recognizing that the game's stylized transformation names do not map literally to on-screen color, so all three converged on the same wrong option.

The rollout that scored 5 (rollout-02) reached the correct letter via a clip_qa answer whose own cited evidence frames (71999.008s/71999.508s) show no transformation at all -- the correct score does not reflect genuine grounded identification of the clue interval; it looks like a coincidental guess.

Rollout-01 never sampled the actual clue window (72210-72223) with clip_qa at all -- its two clip_qa calls stopped at 72030 and 72180 respectively, just short of the transformation onset, so it fell back to an unrelated guess ('dark thunder', apparently tied to a horse-like form seen elsewhere).
what_worked: 4 of 5 rollouts issued clip_qa calls whose time windows did overlap the true clue interval (72210-72223) or came very close, showing the semantic_search/run_sql retrieval steps successfully narrowed the fight down to the right ~72000-72240s window before invoking the visual sub-agent.
transferable_lessons: For 'what does the player transform into' / named-skill-identification questions in a game with stylized (non-literal) Chinese-to-English skill names, do not let the visual sub-agent pick a multiple-choice option purely by matching the observed color to a color-word in the option text -- that heuristic (red/orange -> 'crimson tide') is unreliable when several options could plausibly describe the same visual (e.g. a fire-and-gold effect could be 'golden haze' or 'crimson tide').

When the memory DB text has zero hits for every candidate option word (confirm this cheaply with one run_sql full-text search across episodes/visual_clips before trusting any single clip_qa color-guess), treat all answers as visually-underdetermined and specifically ask clip_qa to look for on-screen skill-name text/icons/notifications near the transformation, not just describe the color of the effect.

A high judge score does not guarantee the reasoning was sound: cross-check the cited evidence_times_s frames of a clip_qa call, not just its verdict -- rollout-02's winning answer cited frames that show no transformation at all.

When two rollouts describe visually near-identical evidence (same fire aura, similar timestamps) but choose different multiple-choice letters, the discriminating signal the model needs (the actual skill name) is probably not present in the sampled frames at all, and more frames of the same color will not resolve it -- look instead for a text/HUD cue or an out-of-band knowledge source.
open_questions: Whether any frame in the 72210-72223 window (not sampled by any rollout's clip_qa) actually contains on-screen Chinese text naming the transformation (e.g. a skill-activation banner) that would have let a rollout read the correct name directly instead of guessing from color -- I sampled frames at 2s granularity myself and saw only combat move prompts (浮光/掠影), not a transformation name banner, but did not exhaustively check every single frame in the interval.

Whether the reference answer 'Golden Haze' is itself derived from external game-knowledge (official skill localization) rather than anything discoverable in this video/DB, which would make the question effectively unanswerable from the given evidence alone for a vision-grounded agent.
